content: [{"id": "hdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Infrastructure", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sthdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Storage", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stintro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Four steps, in the order a file really passes through them. Every upload on this site — a patient's lab report, a partner's attachment, an avatar, a course video — is judged by the same four, because they all sit on the one File record every app on this bench shares.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "st1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Platform File Limits — in System Settings › Files, opened from the sidebar because a tile cannot open a form's tab. These are the platform's own limits, applied before anything below runs: the largest an upload may be, which file types are allowed, and whether anyone but a System Manager may upload a public file. The type list is read from there by the screener too, so a type is allowed or refused in one place rather than two. Left blank, every type is accepted — which is the platform's own default.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "st2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. File Screening — the byte-level checks the platform has not got, run before a single byte reaches storage: the file's opening bytes are matched against the type it claims to be, and its content is scanned by ClamAV. Which verdicts refuse a file, the signatures a type must really begin with, what a scanner outage costs the caller and how long a verdict is kept are all set here, and every field left blank is the shipped default, never nothing. Empty Active Channels screens nothing; screening begins on the channels listed there.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "st3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Azure Blob — where the bytes come to rest once they have been accepted, and the one list of records whose attachments may be public. Everything not named in Public Attachment Doctypes is held private, whatever was ticked in the upload dialog, so a patient's document cannot be made public by choosing to. Left blank, nothing may be public and the display assets that are fetched with no session — profile photos, organisation logos, the login favicon — stop loading.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "st4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Log Settings — the platform's own daily cleanup, and the only place a retention is actually carried out. The scan log is registered there by the screening switch and trimmed at the number of days set on File Screening. While that switch is off the log is not registered at all, so verdicts already written are kept untrimmed until it is turned back on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "None of this runs until its switch is on under Automations: Storage::File::screening, Storage::File::privacy and Storage::Azure::offload each ship dormant, and each is turned on by the operator. What then happened is readable in two places. Every verdict is one row in File Scan Log, accepted as well as blocked, with the reason and the channel it arrived on — a file refused for its bytes and a file refused because the scanner could not be reached are two different rows, and only the second is worth paging anyone about. The files themselves are under Files, each showing the record it belongs to and whether it is private.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stsc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "File Screening", "col": 4}}, {"id": "stsc2", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Azure Storage", "col": 4}}, {"id": "stsc3", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Log Settings", "col": 4}}, {"id": "stsc4", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Files", "col": 6}}, {"id": "stsc5", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "File Scan Log", "col": 6}}, {"id": "lochdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Location", "col": 12}}, {"id": "locsc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Maps", "col": 4}}]
